title: Child Support and Family Assistance Legislation Amendment (Ending Financial Abuse in the Child Support Scheme No. 1) Bill 2026
short_title: Child Support and Family Assistance Legislation Amendment (Ending Financial Abuse in the Child Support Scheme No. 1) Bill 2026

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change child support and family assistance rules, giving the Child Support Registrar new powers over harmful applications, information sharing and payment collection.
It would let either parent request agency collection and expand collection of arrears or refunds arising from retrospective changes to privately collected child support.
Parents in overseas jurisdictions specified by the minister could apply directly for Australian assessments, while existing eligibility rules and standard application requirements would remain.
changes: The Registrar could refuse a payer's assessment application where the prospective recipient does not want it accepted and would face harm.
Objections with little prospect of success or only marginal consequences could be dismissed without full consideration.
Compulsory document exchange would be replaced by discretion over sharing, subject to exchanging information relevant to the decision.
Recovery of certain Family Tax Benefit debts caused by retrospective child support increases would be temporarily paused.
summary.affected: Child support payers, recipients, carers and children are affected.
